text: Home care advice in dengue.
parts: Home care advice in dengue.

text: What to do. Drink adequate fluids. Aim 200 ml of fluid every hour (one small cup) while awake. Examples of fluids include fruit juice, oral rehydration salts (ORS), coconut water, or soup. Take paracetamol for fever or pain when necessary, but not to exceed 4g per day. Get adequate rest. Monitor the temperature and dengue warning signs. Seek immediate medical care if warning signs develop. Attend daily follow-up appointments as advised. Look for mosquito breeding places in and around the home and prevent mosquito bites using mosquito repellent.

text: What to avoid. DO NOT take steroids, aspirin, ibuprofen, diclofenac, or any other NSAIDs. If you are already taking these medications, please consult your doctors. DO NOT consume traditional or herbal remedies. DO NOT take intramuscular injections. DO NOT do massage, cupping or gua sha.

text: Dengue warning signs. As the fever starts to subside, be cautious as the condition may become dangerous and worsen in some dengue patients. Go to the hospital immediately if any of the following occur: General condition worsening or symptoms becoming more severe. Severe abdominal pain. Persistent vomiting. Extreme fatigue. Difficulty breathing or rapid breathing. Fainting spells. Bleeding from the gums or nose, or blood in vomit, urine, or stool. Reduced urine output less than 4 times per day.

text: Nasihat pemantauan demam denggi di rumah.
parts: Nasihat pemantauan demam denggi di rumah.

text: Apa yang perlu dilakukan. Minum air secukupnya sebanyak 200 ml setiap jam (satu cawan kecil) sewaktu jaga. Contoh minuman termasuk jus buah, larutan garam rehidrasi (ORS), air kelapa, atau sup. Ambil paracetamol untuk demam atau sakit badan jika perlu, tetapi tidak melebihi 4g sehari. Dapatkan rehat yang mencukupi. Pantau suhu badan dan tanda amaran demam denggi. Dapatkan rawatan segera jika tanda amaran muncul. Hadiri temujanji susulan. Periksa tempat pembiakan nyamuk di rumah serta cegah gigitan nyamuk menggunakan semburan penghalau nyamuk.

text: Tanda-tanda amaran demam denggi. Apabila demam mula kebah, anda perlu berhati-hati kerana keadaan boleh menjadi berbahaya dan semakin teruk bagi sesetengah pesakit demam denggi. Segera ke hospital jika anda mempunyai salah satu tanda-tanda berikut: Keadaan badan semakin lemah atau simptom semakin teruk. Sakit perut yang teruk. Muntah berterusan. Keletihan melampau. Susah bernafas atau pernafasan laju. Pitam. Pendarahan pada gusi atau hidung, atau darah dalam muntah, air kencing atau najis. Kekerapan kencing kurang dari 4 kali sehari.

text: Cancer pain.
parts: Cancer pain.

text: What causes CANCER PAIN? Cancer pain can result from the tumour pressing on organs, nerves or bones. It may also be caused by cancer treatments like chemotherapy, radiation or surgery.
parts: What causes CANCER PAIN?
Cancer pain can result from the tumour pressing on organs, nerves or bones.
It may also be caused by cancer treatments like chemotherapy, radiation or surgery.

text: Assessing your CANCER PAIN. There are several tools that can be used to assess pain (e.g. Ministry of Health (MoH) Pain Scale). The MoH pain scale combines the NRS, VAS, & faces scale. Patients point to their pain level on a scale from 0 to 10. For children under 7 & cognitively impaired adults, the IASP Faces Pain Scale or FLACC scale may be used. In sedated & intubated patients, pain is assessed through observation including on behaviour. Cancer pain affects not only your physical well-being but also your emotional, social & spiritual health.

For children under 7 & cognitively impaired adults, the IASP Faces Pain Scale or FLACC scale may be used. In sedated & intubated patients, pain is assessed through observation including on behaviour.
Cancer pain affects not only your physical well-being but also your emotional, social & spiritual health.

text: What should I know about PAIN RELIEVING MEDICATIONS? How is cancer pain treated? Cancer pain can be treated using medications (like opioids, non-opioids or adjuvant drugs), physical therapies, psychological & spiritual support & in some cases, interventional procedures. What types of pain medications are available? Medications include: Over-the-counter pain relievers (e.g. paracetamol, ibuprofen); Prescription opioids (e.g. morphine, oxycodone); Adjuvant medications (e.g. antidepressants/ anticonvulsants for nerve pain). Will I become addicted to pain medications? Addiction is rare when opioids are used under medical supervision for cancer pain. Your doctor will prescribe them safely to minimise risks. What are the side effects of pain medications? Common side effects include constipation, nausea, drowsiness, & dizziness. Your doctor can provide treatments to manage these side effects.

text: If I use morphine or other opioids for my pain now, will it be less effective later on when pain gets worse? No, you should not worry about this. Good pain relief will lead to better physical, mental & social well being which will help you cope with your cancer.

text: If I use morphine, does that mean I'm nearing the end of my life? No, taking morphine does not mean you are near the end of life. It is used to manage pain & improve comfort at any stage of cancer. Many people take it for a long time while continuing treatment & daily activities. Talk to your doctor if you have concerns.

text: Where can I get more help for my CANCER PAIN? Contact the following for help & more information. Nearest health clinic/hospital. Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) for pain & palliative care. Malaysian Hospice & Palliative Care Council (MHPCC) (https://www.malaysianhospicecouncil.com/). text: Sakit akibat kanser.
parts: Sakit akibat kanser.

text: Apakah punca SAKIT AKIBAT KANSER? Sakit akibat kanser boleh berlaku apabila ketumbuhan menekan organ, saraf atau tulang. Ia juga boleh disebabkan oleh rawatan kanser seperti kemoterapi, radioterapi atau pembedahan.
parts: Apakah punca SAKIT AKIBAT KANSER?
Sakit akibat kanser boleh berlaku apabila ketumbuhan menekan organ, saraf atau tulang.
Ia juga boleh disebabkan oleh rawatan kanser seperti kemoterapi, radioterapi atau pembedahan.

text: Menilai SAKIT AKIBAT KANSER anda. Terdapat beberapa alat yang boleh digunakan untuk menilai kesakitan (contoh: Ministry of Health (MoH) Pain Scale). MoH pain scale menggabungkan NRS, VAS, & Skala Muka. Pesakit menilai tahap kesakitan mereka pada skala dari 0 hingga 10. Bagi kanak-kanak di bawah 7 tahun & orang dewasa dengan gangguan kognitif, IASP Faces Pain Scale atau FLACC scale boleh digunakan. Bagi pesakit yang tidak sedar & diintubasi, kesakitan dinilai melalui pemerhatian termasuklah ke atas tingkah laku. Sakit kanser bukan sahaja menjejaskan kesejahteraan fizikal anda, tetapi juga kesihatan emosi, sosial & kerohanian.

text: Apa yang perlu saya tahu tentang UBAT MELEGAKAN SAKIT? Bagaimana sakit akibat kanser dirawat? Sakit akibat kanser boleh dirawat dengan ubat-ubatan (seperti opioid, bukan opioid atau ubat adjuvan), terapi fizikal, sokongan psikologi & kerohanian, serta dalam beberapa kes, prosedur khas. Apakah jenis ubat tahan sakit yang ada? Ubat-ubatan termasuk: Ubat tahan sakit tanpa preskripsi (contoh: paracetamol, ibuprofen); Opioid dengan preskripsi (contoh: morfin, oksikodon); Ubat adjuvan (contoh: antidepresan/antikejang untuk sakit saraf). Adakah saya akan menjadi ketagih kepada ubat tahan sakit? Ketagihan jarang berlaku apabila opioid digunakan di bawah pengawasan perubatan untuk sakit kanser. Doktor anda akan mempreskripsikannya dengan selamat bagi mengurangkan risiko. Apakah kesan sampingan ubat tahan sakit? Kesan sampingan biasa termasuk sembelit, loya, mengantuk & pening. Doktor anda boleh memberikan rawatan untuk menguruskan kesan sampingan ini.

text: Jika saya guna morfin atau opioid sekarang, adakah ia kurang berkesan bila sakit saya makin teruk? Tidak, anda tidak perlu risau mengenainya. Kelegaan sakit yang baik akan meningkatkan kesejahteraan fizikal, mental & sosial anda, yang dapat membantu anda mengharungi kanser dengan lebih baik.

Jika anda ada kebimbangan, berbincanglah dengan doktor anda.

text: After a concussion, the patient should be accompanied by a responsible adult if possible. Go to the nearest Emergency Department for: loss of consciousness, disorientation, new deafness, imbalance, blurred or double vision, weakness of any limb, excessive sleepiness or drowsiness, vomiting, bleeding from either ear, fitting, or severe headache not relieved by painkillers. Do stay within reach of a telephone, rest, sleep regularly, and take painkillers such as paracetamol for headache. Don't stay at home alone for 48 hours after leaving hospital.

text: Preventer (budesonide MDI) every day; reliever (salbutamol MDI) when needed. Getting worse (waking at night, worse with a cold): reliever every 4 hours, keep taking the preventer, and come to hospital if not better, bringing the MDI and spacer. Severe (wheeze that does not settle, breathless, hard to talk): come straight to hospital or call an ambulance, taking 4 puffs of the reliever every 4 minutes on the way.

text: Wash the spacer once a week in soapy water, rinse and let it air dry; do not wipe it with a cloth or tissue or brush the inside. Know your triggers: smoke, animal fur, cold air, dust, exercise and infections.

text: Continue taking prescribed medications as directed. Drink plenty of fluid (ORS, clear soups, diluted fruit juices) to prevent dehydration. Avoid caffeinated, alcoholic and sugary drinks, as they can worsen diarrhoea.

text: Get plenty of rest. Hand hygiene, especially after using the toilet and before eating. Seek medical help for persistent vomiting or inability to keep fluids down, blood in stools or persistent high fever, or severe abdominal pain or worsening symptoms.

text: Stay hydrated: drink 6 to 8 glasses of water a day as directed, to help decrease pain and flush blockages from the urinary tract. Strain urine every time you pass urine, and bring any stones passed to the doctor for investigation. Take regular pain medications as directed by the doctor.

text: Seek help at the nearest hospital if pain, fever or vomiting worsens, or for changes in urine: less urine, cloudiness, foul smell. Keep active; kidney stones are more common if you are not active or sit much of the day. Rest, and abstain from alcohol and seafood.

text: Avoid driving, cycling, swimming or heavy machinery for the next 24–48 hours. Hypoglycaemia awareness may be reduced for 48–72 hours: check blood sugar before meals, exercise and driving. Always carry quick-acting carbohydrate (hard candy, dextrose tablets).
